section_heading: Table 1: Course learning outcomes, CO1-CO8
text: Course learning Outcomes (CO) AYPG-AB-PK: CO1 Analyze and apply the core principles of Panchakarma and Upakarma in clinical and wellness practices. CO2 Illustrate and customize standard operating procedures for Panchakarma, Upakarma, Marma Chikitsa, and physiotherapy based on individual patient needs. CO3 Perform Panchakarma and Upakarma procedures, and prepare related formulations with clinical proficiency for both preventive and curative purposes. CO4 Design protocol-based interventions for Panchakarma and Upakarma and demonstrate procedural expertise. CO5 Identify, diagnose, and manage emergencies associated with Panchakarma and Upakarma procedures. CO6 Communicate effectively with all stakeholders. CO7 Integrate recent advances and evidence-based approaches into Panchakarma practice. CO8 Practice and advocate Panchakarma therapy by blending traditional knowledge with modern technology.

document_version: Page update 2021-06-16; Ministry of AYUSH portal
section_heading: Panchakarma definition and five procedures
text: Panchakarma is described as the five therapeutic procedures of Ayurveda associated with bodily purification and dosha elimination: Vamana (therapeutic emesis), Virechana (therapeutic purgation), Basti (medicated enema), Nasya (nasal administration), and Raktamokshana (bloodletting).

section_heading: Panchakarma procedure stages: Poorvakarma, Pradhanakarma, Paschatkarma
text: The Ayusoft reference outlines the three major procedural stages of Panchakarma therapy: Poorvakarma (preparatory procedures including Snehana / oleation and Swedana / sudation), Pradhanakarma (main elimination procedures), and Paschatkarma (post-procedural rehabilitation, dietary regimens including Samsarjana Krama, and lifestyle rules).
